# Testing

Runner: `node --test` (bare - a trailing `test/` path breaks discovery on
Node 22). Suite: 10245 tests across 1026 files.
PROBE (no suite row - it needs `npx wrangler`): `npm run account` (tools/accountProbe.mjs) stands `server-account/` up in a REAL workerd, applies the real migrations to a real D1 through wrangler's ledger, and drives the whole account lifecycle AND (AUDIT-312 F4) a whole cloud-save round trip against workerd's own R2 - 36 checks. IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE SUITE WAS GREEN OVER A WORKER THAT COULD NOT BOOT: a module Worker reads every named export of its entrypoint as an entrypoint, `server-account/src/index.js` exported four constants, and workerd refused to start - while `test/accountworker.test.js` passed BECAUSE it imported those very names. Importability is not deployability. It also measures what the suite can only assume: Ed25519 exists in that runtime (it is not in every WebCrypto and the token design rests on it), PBKDF2 at 210,000 costs 36ms there, and a token the Worker SIGNS verifies against the key the Worker PUBLISHES, with a stranger's key and a bent byte as the negative controls. AUDIT-312 F4 ADDED ACC2's HALF, and the reason is the same one: ACC2 declared a new BINDING (`SAVES`, an R2 bucket) and seven routes, and nothing in this tree asked whether that binding is really bound - a binding that is ABSENT does not crash, it answers `no-storage`, which reaches a player as "Cloud saves are unavailable right now" with a green suite and a green deploy behind it. It drives the guest wall, a blob refused without a card, the card, the bytes back BYTE FOR BYTE as an octet-stream, the shot bounded apart from the save, another account refused a read and a delete, and the player's own delete taking the object as well as the row. AND IT WAS ONLY EVER CORRECT ONCE: `wrangler --local` REUSES its state, so run two registered a username run one had taken and logged in with a password run one's recovery check had changed - six failures about the last run rather than about the service, and a migration check reading "no migrations to apply" as "no migrations". It stands on a fresh `--persist-to` directory now, and two runs back to back are 36/36 twice. AND IT HAS BEEN MUTATED AT LAST (AUDIT-PW, tools/mutants/acctprobe.json, 4, 4 dead) - AUDIT-ACC named this tool as never-mutated beside password.js and it stayed that way for a day. The question a campaign asks of a PROBE is the inverse of the usual one: break the SERVICE, and does the probe go red? All four do, and TWO OF THEM THE SUITE CANNOT SEE AT ALL - a named value export back on the entrypoint (the original bug: workerd refuses to start over a constant while the suite stays green BECAUSE it imports those very names) and the R2 binding renamed in wrangler.toml (the suite hands the Worker its own env and never reads that file). The other two are a hash cost that leaves a Worker's CPU budget, which only a real runtime can time, and a migration that stops applying through wrangler's own ledger, which is the thing the deploy runs. `--local` is workerd, not Cloudflare: no network, no D1 limit, no cold start. Set ACCOUNT_PROBE_PORT if a previous run left an orphan. PROBE (no suite row - it needs a browser): `node tools/quickLootStatsProbe.mjs` draws the quick-loot plaque AND its stat panel through `showWorldPlaque` - the same seam the four hosts call - over the real ENHANCED_CSS in Chromium, at desktop, narrow and phone widths, walking the highlight down a pile of four, and photographs each. It exists because a player asked for the stats "next to the quickloot window" and NEXT TO is a thing about pixels: the suite can say the side was COMPUTED right and never that the panel reads as one surface with the list beside it. CHARGEN-REFLEX's lesson is built in - the markup is the real `paint`'s, not the probe's, because a harness that writes its own markup measures its own artefact. IT PAID FOR ITSELF ON THE FIRST RUN, TWICE, on faults no pin in the suite could have failed on: a Condition reads "Slightly Used (75%)" and the panel is deliberately narrow, so that row WRAPS - and the value was only pushed right by an auto margin, so its second line sat hard against the LABEL and read as a different row; and the survival SENTENCE rows ("Nourishes for 180 minutes") inherited the fix's right alignment and read as a value with no name. The rows were right, the side was right, the markup was right, and the box looked wrong. 12 shots. PROBE (no suite row - it runs 600 frames of the real rig): `node tools/peerBodiesProbe.mjs` drives the REAL PeerBodies over the REAL `createFpArm` rig on the arm fixtures with a counting renderer - 1, 4 and 8 peers walking out from 4 m to 50 m, a pose every sixth frame - and reports poses+uploads and sprite renders a body a frame. It exists because PERF-ON2 measured the online frame and never the peer bodies, which are its one real cost; it read 1.00 poses a body a frame at every count before PEER-CADENCE and 0.74 / 0.52 / 0.43 after, and still 1.00 sprite renders, which is the open item. The fixture rig is four small pieces, so its milliseconds are not a retail body's; the counts are exact. PROBE (no suite row - it needs a browser): `node tools/chatFitProbe.mjs` stands the REAL chat panel (createChatPanel over a real ChatLog, CHAT_CSS over the enhanced sheet) in Chromium at a desktop and a phone-landscape viewport with twenty-four long names wearing titles and glyphs, and MEASURES: the box is 299 px with three names and 299 px with twenty-four, the column exactly as tall as the conversation, 437 px of list in 235, every row one line (16-17 px against a 16.2 px line), eight names cut with an ellipsis, and the chat lines wearing their authors' badges. It exists because Mac's report was a screenshot and every one of its three sentences is about pixels: a pin can say a rule reads `nowrap` and a column is `absolute`, and only a layout engine can say the box stopped growing. 12 checks, 2 shots. PROBE (no suite row - it needs a browser): `node tools/noticeFitProbe.mjs` draws the enhanced NOTICE PANELS through `drawEnhancedNotice` - the entry every box and every toast goes through - over the real ENHANCED_CSS in Chromium, at desktop, narrow and phone widths, and MEASURES each one's border-box width: a one-line notice, the status readout, a long quest box and a toast come back 210 / 450 / 520 / 339 px at 1280 wide, four widths where NOTICE-FIT found one. It exists because kurkku asked for "the sizing of the boxes to properly adjust for the text" and width is a thing about pixels - a pin can say the rule reads `max-width` and still not say that "You are healthy." hugs its line while a four-paragraph box still wraps at the cap. IT LIED ON ITS FIRST RUN and the picture is how it was caught: the panels photographed 46px off the right edge with a live transform, because NOTICE_WATCHDOG_MS had correctly swept a panel nobody was drawing - a harness that does not do what the host does measures its own artefact, so it PUMPS the draw on rAF the way a host does. 12 measurements, 3 shots. PROBE (no suite row - it needs a browser): `npm run blood` (tools/bloodProbe.mjs) drives `createHitEffects` and `drawBillboards` over a texture whose colour is known, in a real WebGL2 context, and reads the pixel back at five lighting states. MAC-BUG W6: and then installs the Enhanced Lighting lane and reads a sprite and a mark side by side at four more - the rows where the mark came back at 25 against 69 and 2 against 17 while every classic row was green. 26 checks (AUDIT BLOOD3 F10: and the MENISCUS is drawn now - the same mark against a uniform-thickness one under a grazing sun, the difference banded by radius, which is the one law this arc took to main with no picture; the film's own rows, banded by RADIUS inside the mark's silhouette rather than by brightness, which was sorting the alpha-faded rim into the thin bucket and measuring the blend). It exists because MAC-BUG W4 ("Also blood is black") could not be settled by reading: it clears the pool, the texture KEY (`380_0#0` is minted in scenes/dataPipeline.js and asked for in render/renderer.js, and nothing had ever checked the two agree), the shader's emission arm, and anything specific to blood - a plain sprite in the same dungeon light comes back the same 20,2,2. 9 checks.

**THE ARENA2-GATED PINS ARE HALF-BLIND, AND THAT IS A KNOWN COST.** A
pin behind `{ skip: skipReal }` never runs on CI, so a law change that
contradicts it goes unnoticed until someone runs the suite WITH game
data. Two did (2026-08-23, found while merging the input arc):
audit18_hosts_dungeon's swing-fatigue pin still asserted the drain
AUDIT 24 wave 42 had deliberately moved to the hosts, and
cityguards.test.js's stub renderer lacked the `destroyBillboardBatch`
wave 6's batch-free calls - it THREW rather than failed. Both are
fixed, and both by making the pin say MORE, not less. When you change
a law, grep the ARENA2-gated files for it too.

**AND THEY ARE ENGLISH-RETAIL-LOCKED, WHICH NOTHING SAID.** 2026-08-25:
the gated pins ran in a working environment for the first time, against
a real ARENA2 pulled from the DaggerfallSetup installer. 35 of them
failed, and NONE of the 35 is a port defect. 8 fail on FILENAME CASE
alone - retail data was written on a filesystem that did not care, and
that install carries `INVE00I0.img` beside `INVE04I0.IMG` and
`ANIM0001.vid` beside `ANIM0002.VID`, 76 lowercase names among 1,598.
The shipping data path already knew (`dataSource.normalizeName`
uppercases on both ingest and lookup, so the browser is fine); the test
harness and the vite dev middleware read the folder case-sensitively,
so `npm run dev` 404'd against files that were sitting right there.
The dev server is case-insensitive now; the pins still read the folder
literally and a mixed-case corpus still reddens them.

The other 27 are LOCALISATION. That install is the German edition, and
these pins encode the English retail corpus by value: FACTION.TXT has
374 records against the pinned 366 and names faction 41 Kriegergilde,
the map directory has no location called "Privateer's Hold" so five
dungeon pins dereference null, SPELLS.STD's indices move, CLASS*.CFG
carries different career flags (a Mage there CAN wear plate), and the
IMG corpus is 198 files against 263. Every one of those is the data
being legitimately different, not the port being wrong.

Two port-relevant facts fell out of the same run and are recorded
rather than fixed, because both change shipped behaviour: the
CLASS*.CFG NAME FIELD IS ENCIPHERED in that edition (CLASS00 reads
"vfu", CLASS15 reads "dfhdfh" - a repeated three-gram where German's
Barbar is a repeated three-gram, so the record parses correctly and
only the name is coded) and `chargenSession` falls back to
CLASS_CAREERS only when the name is EMPTY, so a non-English install
shows gibberish in the class list; and the port's font maps the
high-bit range to punctuation, so every umlaut renders as `#` or `}`
("St#rke", "W}ste"). Neither can be caught by any pin the suite has,
because the suite has never had non-English data.

Pinned by restoring the exact broken line and watching it fail. TDZ2 (HOTFIX 2026-09-19) is the SAME ERROR THROWN ACROSS TWO MODULES, by a third party who touched neither: `ui/hud.js` and `ui/enhancedHud.js` have imported each other for most of this port's life, and enhancedHud has long re-exported hud's `compassScroll` - both harmless. The third ingredient is a NAMESPACE over one of them (a dynamic `import()` or an `import * as`), because a namespace object is built by READING EVERY BINDING AT ONCE, so it reaches through the re-export into the other module's `const` while that module is still initialising. LV2's lab asked for one, and `/play/` went black for every player with "can't access lexical declaration 'yv' before initialization". NOTHING IN THE GATE COULD SEE IT - every module imports cleanly under node because no namespace is built there, the build succeeds, and 9030 tests passed; only the BUNDLE throws, and only at boot. The third ingredient is the one a slice adds, so the third is what is pinned. |

TTL1 (2026-09-20, the creator relayed by Mac: "Spawned Dungeons should expire/removed after 2 ingame days when cleared when there is no player in it - and after 7 ingame days in general when there is no player in it"). TWO CLOCKS, and a spawn dies on whichever runs out first: a SHORT one started by the clearing and a LONG one running since first sight. Clearing does not extend a life - a spawn cleared on day 6 of its seven is gone on day 7, not day 8 - so the test is an OR, not a fork. Both are in the game’s own classic minutes, so resting through a week expires what a week of walking would, and a NEGATIVE elapsed is never expiry because loading an older save winds the clock BACK. "No player in it" is kept at the one place a pixel is rebuilt (buildPixelNow): a dungeon freezes the streamer’s pixel at the ENTRANCE, and a spawn is entered from its own pixel, so the entrance pixel IS the spawn’s key - no map id needs comparing. The short clock is started by the dungeon context, which tells the host once when every foe is dead and every pile empty, on a slow throttle piggybacked on automapTick AHEAD of that scan’s own early return. The ledger rides EVERY save through composeSessionState - not the `world` bag, which is written in exterior mode alone, and a spawn’s clock is counting exactly where a player saves; a pre-TTL1 save loads an empty ledger and every spawn simply starts its seven days over. Pinned on the table of both clocks, the once-only starts, the save round trip and the source of all four seams. The two are held against each other anyway, by reading the four sRGB numbers back OUT of the shader text - if the GLSL curve ever moves, the host's must move with it. The cache is keyed on the display triple it was made from, starts at NaN (a zero triple would match a legitimately black fog and never recompute, and that mutant dies), owns its own scratch rather than `_c3`'s - which is handed to whoever asks next - and is INVALIDATED ON A LANE SWAP, because a cache keyed on its input alone cannot see that the function changed. The far ring is named as an asymmetry rather than an oversight: it pastes the same block but has its own finish and its own upload path, so it keeps its own decode. The port’s own blood marks. The FEEL is measured off DaggerBlood 1.0.6a (Excoriated) and NOTHING ELSE is - no code, no art, no vendor row, no `[IL]` citation into his assembly anywhere in this tree (bible/05-Combat/Blood-Arc.md carries the whole of that reasoning). What these pins hold are the FACTS the reading established, which are numbers and orderings rather than anybody’s expression, and the port’s own maths around them. THE RATE LADDER: three rungs with a ceiling of their own (25/30, 50/50, 100/70), then the near-lethal 150, then 200 - and the top rung’s boundary IS the overkill line, one number rather than a fourth table row, so the two cannot drift apart. THE DENSITY FLOOR is `max(1, ...)`: a player who turns the blood right down gets less of it and never none of it. OVERKILL IS 175%, not the 200 the reference’s own setting text claims - the text rounds and the code does not - and the pin drives 172.5% and 175% either side of it. THE POOL IS A COUNT AND NOT A LIFETIME: a fixed ring that hands back the OLDEST slot forever, so the cost of blood is decided at boot and cannot grow during a fight. A mark is lifted 2cm ALONG ITS SURFACE’S NORMAL (the same nudge hitEffects.js gives its splash), so a wall’s mark comes off the wall; the streaming world’s recentre moves every live mark on all three axes, and the pin’s delta carries a height term because a zero one would let a dropped y pass. THE SURFACE BASIS is pinned for validity over five normals AND for STABILITY: the seed axis swaps near horizontal not because the maths breaks (the collapse falls to a valid fallback) but because just beside the collapse the cross product is ill-conditioned - two floors tilted a thousandth either way would disagree about which way is right, and a dungeon floor is never exactly level. And the module knows NO RENDERER: the source is read for `renderer`, `gl.`, `drawScreenQuad`, `uploadTexture` and even `import`, because the camp.js/camps.js split is what lets every law above be driven on a table. THE DRAW came with the same slice: a decal is FOUR CORNERS around its own centre, and the corner maths is pinned here rather than in a GL context because that is where its bugs are - size is the FULL width, every corner sits at the half-diagonal and LIES IN THE PLANE of the surface (no component along the normal), the uv order says BL/TL/TR/BR and the index buffer is wound to match, opposite corners straddle the centre, the tint rides PER VERTEX so one call draws marks of different colours, and AN EMPTY SLOT IS A ZERO-AREA QUAD rather than a gap - the ring is drawn whole in one call, so a hole has to be something the rasteriser throws away instead of something the draw skips, which would cost either a call per run of live decals or an index rebuild on every placement. Mutants: 17, 17 dead. Blood over open air past MARK_DROP leaves nothing rather than a mark hanging in space. A BLOODLESS FOE STAINS NOTHING, off DFU’s own bloodIndex. A room thrown away takes its blood on the `clear()` every host already makes, and its GL on `dispose()`. THE MARK’S ART IS THE SPLASH’S SETTLED FRAME: a splash plays out to the stain and then vanishes, so that last frame IS the mark, recorded at the upload because nothing else can see `frameCount` - the port ships NO blood picture and the pin greps for one. THE SHAFT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT — the reference reads the LIVE weapon state when blood spawns, which for an arrow that has been in the air is whatever the player’s arm happens to be doing now, a quirk of reading a global at spawn time rather than a thing to carry. THEN AN AUDIT OF THE WHOLE ARC (2026-09-20, Mac: “Lets do a comprehensive audit on everything so far”), WHICH FOUND THE ONE THAT MATTERED: BLOOD NEVER APPEARED INSIDE BUILDINGS. `worldModes.js` builds an interior pool like the other three hosts, hands it to the splash pool, ticks it every frame and clears it on the way out — and never once DREW it, so every mark laid in a shop, a tavern or a house was computed, written into a GPU buffer and never rendered. The comment three lines above that pool reads “the whole payload — sound, knockback, death, corpse, loot AND the splash — runs indoors exactly as it does in the other three hosts”. AND THE PIN ABOVE IS WHY IT WENT UNSEEN: it counts four draws, and the fourth is worldModes drawing the DUNGEON’S pool (`dungeonCtx.bloodMarks.draw`). Nothing asked whether worldModes drew its OWN. Four hosts, four pools, three draws, and a pin that counted to four on the wrong objects. The replacement is by BINDING rather than by count — it walks `src/`, finds every `const X = createBloodMarks(`, and holds that each X is DRAWN by that same name and UNDER its host’s own sprites. A fifth pool built next year fails on the day it is written. THREE MORE THE AUDIT TURNED UP. DISPOSE WAS NOT TERMINAL: a `place` or `tick` arriving after teardown — a peer’s blow over the wire as the room goes, a splash whose art resolved late — ran `ensure()` and minted a fresh ring and a fresh GPU batch on a pool nobody would ever free again, which is the HARD1 fault from the other end (not a thing freed twice, but a thing BUILT after its owner had gone). THE ART COULD ARRIVE AFTER THE THROW: `_gibArt` is set when a splash’s texture resolves, and on the FIRST blood of a session that lands after `place` has already thrown — so the batch was built with no art and nothing ever built it again, and a player whose first blood was a warhammer overkill watched ten invisible chunks fly. AND `[].every()` IS TRUE, so with no chunks and a drip still falling the bare guard reseated on every frame of the fall; it no-opped, which is how it went unseen, and the mutation of it is recorded EQUIVALENT rather than pinned because nothing outside the pool can observe it. The flight also stopped allocating: the chunks’ centre list is built once with the batch and is the chunks’ OWN `pos` arrays, which every writer mutates in place — pinned both ways, that the frame builds no list and that no writer replaces an array, since a replaced one would leave every chunk drawing at its birthplace for ever. The renderer’s sphere is walked in place too, into the batch’s own array, and the pin now holds BOTH terms of the radius after a mutant that dropped the centres’ extent survived the first cut. It was never caught because with NO light the two passes AGREE - the fault appears the moment there is anything to see by, which is where a player is looking. The pin holds the SHAPE a suite can hold: the decal shader's point-light loop is compared CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER against the billboard shader's (the same regex matched against both, so neither can drift without the other), the indirect term beside it, the three summed rather than one used, and the upload's sun-half, point count and light arrays - with AUDIT PERF-SUN/FOG F4's three-colours-three-scratches rule honoured rather than rediscovered, and a clockless scene zeroing its sun so it cannot carry the last one's. The colour is a PURE SCALE: BLOOD_BASE is its old self times 0.81 on all three channels, so G/R is 0.085 where it was 0.086 - "a tad darker" is a luminance note and re-mixing by eye would have answered a question nobody asked. The pin that held it was a bare `> 0.5` threshold; it is re-aimed onto the law (inside the curve, red by a wide margin, the hue held, and DARKER than the red it replaced). THE SAMENESS HAD TWO CAUSES AND THE OBVIOUS ONE WAS THE SMALLER. A wall mark is always the `drip` kind and always near-plumb - it has to be, a run runs downward - so it has none of the freedom the floor's marks take from the throw: four cells were four pictures for ever. Doubling ATLAS_CELLS to 8 (the sheet 512 wide, the cell still 64) was the obvious half; the pin that MEASURED it found the drips at IoU 0.96 against each other, because `shapeAt`'s drip had exactly two degrees of freedom and neither moved the bead, the column or the foot. So the shape gained the freedoms a real run has: where the bead struck and how big, WHETHER IT RAN AT ALL (a third never do - the biggest break in the every-mark-has-a-tail sameness), how far, a sideways drift the foot follows, and a fork. Worst overlap is 0.76 now and the covered area spans 244 to 581 where it spanned 370 to 410. `pickCell` mirrors horizontally on top (16 faces a kind, a NEW object every time - the cells are shared by every mark on the wall), and `WALL_RUN_LEAN` lets a run sit up to seven degrees off plumb, both ways. THE DEPTH WAS THE CATCH: the first cut took it from the run alone, which gave the bead, the foot and every pixel of a no-run cell a thickness of ZERO - the deep end inside out - and BLOOD3's own depth pin caught it in one line. A drop is a DOME: its alpha ends at a hard rim, its thickness feathers to nothing just inside. The new pin measures distinctness by OVERLAP rather than by a coverage-and-centroid proxy (which two near-identical drips pass), drives the lean over a sample big enough to tell two-way from one-way, and holds the dome through `filmThickness`. Five blood1 and blood3 records re-aimed by content. Twelve mutations, twelve dead - three of them survivors first, which is how the no-run case, the dome and the lean's direction got pinned at all. |

| boot1.test.js | 2 | BOOT1 (2026-09-20, Mac: "overall performance improvements"): THE GAME HOSTS ARE BEHIND A DOOR, NOT ON THE ENTRY. src/main.js imported all four scene hosts statically, which put the whole game - 623 of the tree's files, 13.4 MB of source - on the boot path before boot() ran a line, while the MENU the player sees first was the thing behind a dynamic import. The first pin does not read main.js's import lines; it WALKS the entry's static import graph transitively, exactly as the bundler will, and holds that no host is on it - a regex on the lines would go vacuous the day any other module on the entry imported a host on main.js's behalf. The hosts are DERIVED (every src/scenes file exporting a boot door), each must still be reachable by its dynamic door calling that export, and a ceiling holds the entry's reach under 60% of the tree so the graph cannot quietly re-invert. The second pin is the warm-up: the world host's import starts BEFORE the menu is awaited (or it downloads after the player has clicked Play), names the same file the door boots, and carries a catch - a deploy between page load and Play renames every chunk, and a warm-up that rejected unhandled would be a console error for a failure the real import reports properly. Measured over the build: the chunks a browser must fetch before the entry finishes evaluating went from 54 (1,349 KB gzipped) to 28 (492 KB). THE TWO MODE CYCLES DISAGREE, and it is DFU's own: PlayerActivate.NextInteractionMode walks the enum (Steal > Grab > Info > Talk) and the panel walks Steal > TALK > GRAB > Info, so clicking the bar's mode button and pressing the mode key move through the same four modes in different orders - reusing the keyboard's cycle passes any "it cycles" pin and dies here. The right click is the exact inverse of the panel's own, round-tripped from every mode. DOCKED collapses AutoSizeModes.ScaleToFit's arithmetic to the screen's full width in proportion, flush to the bottom (an integer-floored scale leaves a gap and fails); UNDOCKED is the native scale times LargeHUDUndockedScale with alignment None FORCED to Centre, so 0 and 2 are the same bar. The compass frame is a C# `(int)` TRUNCATION over 32 frames, walked at 401 headings to prove nothing indexes past the last, with the port's wrap covering the 1.0 DFU's own read can never produce. Only the MAP and INTERACTION-MODE panels differ on the right button (the automap left and the travel map right; the mode cycle forward and back); the other nine bind ONE handler to both, which is checked from the other side. And every panel posts an ACTION ui/input.js routes - the same door the keyboard uses, driven through a recording ctx - with the five arms U45 added reporting honestly when no host has grown a door and the four that predate it returning true regardless, pinned as the inconsistency it is. Plus the four-hosts wiring: all four DRAW the bar, and the four that own a pointer offer it the click and bind ActivateCursor. 11 mutations, 11 killed + D10 shipped the two OFFSETS this subject used to record as read by nothing: horseOffsetHeight is the drawn bar's height and NEVER asks about docking (TransportManager.cs:304-309, the (int) truncation included), weaponOffsetHeight is FORCED whenever the bar is docked whatever the setting says (FPSWeapon.cs:146-155) and consults the setting only undocked, both answer 0 on a null HUD, and the offset really moves the horse rect (moved, not resized) and the viewmodel quad. X2 PARITY (the three gaps the X1 review left open): absorption recomputing its chance from the TARGET level at absorb time while resistance stays frozen at the CASTER level (DFU's one asymmetry - TryEffectBasedAbsorption reads entity.Level, TryResistance goes through RollChance/ChanceValue), both reading ONE incumbent rather than a sum (a 50%% item beside a 50%% spell used to read as a certainty) while Elemental Resistance keeps its genuine additive sum, and all three riding AssignBundle's no-magnitude saving throw so a non-CasterOnly defence buff can be refused WHOLE while a self-cast never is. | staticnpc.test.js | 8 | NPC1 - StaticNPC.cs's identity layer, the data under every person standing in a shop, temple, guild hall or palace. Classic stores no NPC table: a person IS their position and their faction, and their name, gender, race and portrait all fall out of those two through a seeded PRNG - which is why the same shopkeeper is the same person every time you walk in and why they differ between one building and the next. THREE PINS EARN THEIR KEEP. The NAME SEED is `position ^ buildingKey + locationIndex`, and C# binds + tighter than ^, so it groups as position ^ (buildingKey + locationIndex) - the natural left-to-right reading renames every NPC in the game, and the pin's inputs are chosen so the two groupings DISAGREE (the first draft used a triple where they coincide and would have passed against the wrong one). FACTION.TXT's race column is a DIFFERENT enum from Races, not an offset of it - FactionRaces is Nord 0, Khajiit 1, Redguard 2, Breton 3... where Races is Breton 1, Redguard 2, Nord 3... so the orders disagree as well as the bases, and "the same list one lower" is wrong for every entry but one; the port's first draft computed exactly that and every NPC would have taken the wrong race with the suite green. And the position hash is pinned to LITERAL values, because re-deriving the formula inside the assertion pins nothing - it passes against any implementation that matches itself. Plus gender being flag bit 32 and nothing else, an INDIVIDUAL faction answering its own name where everyone else is seeded and STABLE, an unfactioned person taking the race of the region (which is what makes a village look like its province), and the four FACTION.TXT races with no Races counterpart falling through to that same fallback |

THE ELEMENT IS TWO HALVES THAT MUST NOT BE CONFUSED, and nearly every way it can go wrong is one behaving like the other: an ANNOUNCEMENT is an event and expires, a REMINDER is a STATE and lasts exactly as long as the level is unspent. So the pins drive the queue (a second raise of the same skill UPDATES its row rather than stacking - a strip is not a log; the cap drops the oldest chatter and never the level, because a rest raises a handful of skills in one pass and the row a player is looking for must not be the one pushed off; the level's row is drawn LAST so the one row that asks for something does not move when raiseSkills raises the skills and THEN levels the player), the two lives of the level's row (news, then a fold to a reminder that says something ELSE - a reminder still calling itself news is how a player learns to stop reading the strip), and the arm a latch would have got wrong: a level spent by ANY road - the window, the font-less escape, a headless roll, a load - takes the reminder with it, because the paint reads `entity.readyToLevelUp` live rather than remembering that it announced one. A level owed but never announced here still says so. ONE EVENT, ONE FANFARE: the strip plays it where the level was earned and the door asks `fanfareOwed` before the window, which may not open for another ten minutes, plays it again - and a SECOND level earned while the first is unspent still sounds. THE FORK IS WRITTEN ONCE: all four hosts announce through the seam and none opens a window from a level-up arm, every `open` thunk is still the host's own, and the classic lane is byte-for-byte what it was (the line, the sheet, the mastery's click-anywhere box). The key the strip names is the REGISTRY's, through `codeForAction` - the inverse of `actionForCode`, in one home beside it - because a rebound key named by its default is FIX-F's bug one layer down. THE MUTANT THAT SURVIVED THE FIRST SUITE is why the three seams take a `doc`: under node every call took the classic arm and the arm this whole slice is about was unreachable, so "the window opens itself again" could not be failed by anything. LV3 (2026-09-19, Dudey: "a button to open the levelup screen again once closed") makes the strip's LEVEL ROW a button. It presses the SHEET KEY through ui/levelUpOpener.js rather than reaching into a host: there are four hosts, each with its own slot and key ladder, and every one already answers the CharacterSheet action by mounting the door - a button that reached into one would be three more places to forget it. It is the touch layer's own idiom ("A TOUCH CONTROL PRESSES AN ACTION, NOT A LETTER") and it takes that idiom's refusal with it: an UNBOUND sheet action presses nothing and draws no button, because a button that fires whatever key used to be there would press some other action's. The strip is pointer-events:none so it never eats a click meant for the world; this one row opts back in, and a skill line stays a plain div because a report is not a door. Two tiers per module:
1. **Synthetic fixtures** - in-memory data built inside the test. Always run;
   CI stays green with no game data (88 pass, 49 skip).
2. **Real-data validation** - gated on `ARENA2_PATH`; skip cleanly when
   absent. Pin observed counts, names, ids, checksums, and structural
   closure invariants.

Without game data the suite runs 805 pass / 120 skip (AUDIT 18 corrected
the long-stale "88 pass, 49 skip", which described a 137-test suite that
has not existed for many milestones). Those 75 skipped pins DO NOT RUN
IN THE DEPLOY GATE - CI has no ARENA2 - so a real-data pin is a local
gate only. (Measured on main at the AUDIT 18 merge; recount by hand
when the split moves.) `manifest.test.js` guards the totals above but not this line;
recount it by hand when the split moves.

Sourcing data in a fresh session: `sh tools/fetch-data.sh`, then
`ARENA2_PATH=/home/claude/dfdata/arena2 npm test`.

Visual proof: `npm run shot [out.png]` boots vite in-process and drives the
provisioned Chromium (playwright@1.56.0 <-> /opt/pw-browsers chromium-1194;
bump both together). CONTRACT: the scene query rides the SHOT_QUERY env
var, NOT argv (`SHOT_QUERY='shot&world&tod=22:00' npm run shot out.png`) -
argv[2] is only the output path. SHOT_TIMEOUT overrides the 30s ready
wait (streaming world wants 90000); SHOT_EVAL runs a JS snippet in-page
after ready (promise-returning expressions are awaited - top-level
`await` fails). Shot-mode probe hooks in the dungeon and world scenes:
window.__move(dx, dy, dz), window.__pose(x, y, z, yaw, pitch),
window.__player {pos, warp}, and in the dungeon __activate/__activateKey/
__ray/__actions. SwiftShader renders heavy scenes at ~7 fps headless -
time-based proofs must poll state, never trust wall-clock. `?shot` in main.js fixes the vantage and raises
`window.__shotReady`. Manual proof, not a suite gate.

Playing the game: `ARENA2_PATH=... npm run firsthour` drives ONE character
through one continuous session on the real hosts - chargen, the starting
dungeon, a fight, the loot, the way out, the road, a town, a shop, a
purchase, a bed - asserting the player is alive and the state coherent at
each step, with a screenshot per stage (`SHOTS=<dir>`, default
`firsthour-shots/`). A failing stage does NOT stop the walk; its dependents
are marked skipped and the run continues, because the output is a MAP of
what a first hour hits rather than the first pothole. `ONLY_CHARGEN=1` stops
after the wizard - a four-minute run instead of twenty-five, which is how
the modal-ownership fix was red-proofed. It is a TOOL, not a suite gate: it
needs game data and about twenty-five minutes of SwiftShader. Run it when a
host, a window or the boot path changes - `tools/nativeTradeProbe.mjs` sat
red for months because nothing did.

PX31 (2026-08-31) found the same rot ACROSS THE FLEET, and one line up
from any assertion: NINE probes waited on `#enhanced-menu .railbtn` at
their front door. `railbtn` is the SHELL rail's class and the boot door
has not carried one since PX1 replaced it with the pixel home, whose
buttons were classless - so every one of them timed out before its
first check, and had since 2026-08-27. The fix is a hook rather than
nine text selectors: the door's buttons carry `doorbtn door-<id>` and
the probes select on that, because matching on the visible words would
be the same bug waiting on a relabel. Opening the door then showed the
rot goes deeper in at least two of them - `enhancedPackProbe` and
`enhancedDollProbe` still assert the U53 slot map (`.node`,
`.node.filled`) that PX19d and PX20a replaced with the worn map. Those
bodies are a repair of their own and are NOT done, which is why PX31's
own pin is a new file (`tools/enhancedPackLayoutProbe.mjs`) rather than
more checks bolted to a probe that cannot reach them.

THE STANDING LESSON IS SHARPER THAN "RUN THE PROBES": a probe that
cannot reach its first check fails identically to a probe nobody ran,
and neither shows up anywhere. A red probe is evidence; an unreachable
one is silence wearing evidence's clothes.

Pre-push gate: `npm run check` (test + build).

Drift guard: `test/manifest.test.js` pins the total line and every row of
the table above against the real suite. Recalculate this doc in the same
commit as any test change.

NEITHER GATES THE MAGIC: a missing spellcast group is a note on the card and the spell still flies. | modsettings.test.js | 7 | ROADS 24 (2026-09-02): A VENDORED MOD'S OWN SWITCHES. DFU's settings model is its 171 keys and nothing else, so a mod's switches live in systems/modSettings.js - keyed by vendor folder, the mod's own names, defaults and descriptions as its modsettings ships them (SmoothRoads on, RiversAndStreams off), through the port's one storage seam - shown under the mod's name on the Mods pane, and carried on the network object into the kernel on BOTH paths (his data and the fallback). The editor switches are not carried. THE SECOND IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE LAW and is the one the rule’s first cut needed: an honestly SMALL dungeon still caches. That cut measured against the voxelizer’s own box count, and a tall thin wall voxelizes into far more boxes than its floor does, so a perfectly healthy little room tripped it; the guard measures `input.tris`, the same stable count the cache key is built from, and is gated on a genuinely large input so a real small dungeon is never touched. The three numbers are NAMED (`DEGENERATE_MIN_TRIS`, `DEGENERATE_MIN_POLYS`, `DEGENERATE_POLY_SHARE`) because together they ARE the rule, and the pins read them rather than repeating them. It was PAINTED OVER. `.choose` is centred at `height: 100%` and `.stagebody`'s implicit grid row is `auto` (max-content), so a stage taller than the pane kept its full height while `.stagebody` shrank under `flex: 1; min-height: 0` - and the difference spilled out of the bottom as VISIBLE overflow, under the opaque `.actionbar` laid out straight after it. Reflexes is the ONLY `.choose` stage with a Continue (sex, class method and biography method all advance on the ANSWER) and the tallest, five answers at `min-height: 88px` = 748px, so it is the only one that could strand a player and nothing measured it. MEASURED, because node cannot see a painted rectangle: tools/chargenReflexProbe.mjs reads `document.elementFromPoint` at the button's own centre in a real browser at eight window sizes - at 1280x720 it answers `DIV.actionbar`, and below 768 tall the button is outside the viewport entirely, while 1920x1080 is green, which is why nobody developing on a big screen ever saw it. SHOW_BUG=1 re-proves the shipped-before state red at five sizes. THE FIX IS TWO HALVES: `.stagebody` rows become `minmax(0,1fr)` so the row can give way, and `.choose` takes `place-content: safe center` + `overflow-y: auto` (plain `center` is a trap - centred overflow goes BOTH ways and the half above the start edge can never be scrolled to); and the wizard's primary action is DECLARED by the stage and drawn by the action bar, which is a sibling of the scrolling stage and always on screen. The three stages on the MANDATORY path are converted (name, the biography rep box, reflexes); four short card panes still draw their own primary and are named in a KNOWN list that may shrink and never grow, so a new offender fails. SquidKamer: "Respawn after poison and likely disease and other things can cause a deathloop... Its basically permanent death for your character." trashBattery: "Dying while falling with guards nearby to arrest you will place you in a deathloop once your jail sentence ends. You cannot access a menu while in this mode. The only way to stop the game now is to force-kill the process." MAC-D3 FIXED THE ORDER OF THE REVIVAL AND NOT ITS CONTENT: it moved the heal to the top so no frame could see a dead player with no death screen, which closed the window between reviving and landing. This is the other half - the health came back and THE CAUSE DID NOT GO AWAY, so a poisoned character woke at half health and the poison emptied it again in seconds. THE LINE IS DRAWN ON RATE: poison, continuous damage and health transfer tick on the COMBAT ROUND and are cleared; a disease's HEA column falls once per CLASSIC DAY, which is days of walking at half health - enough to reach the temple that cures it - so diseases are KEPT, and they must be, because vampirism and lycanthropy are carried as `kind: 'disease'` entries (systems/infection.js) and a blanket cure would make dying on purpose the cheapest cure in the game. THE SECOND REPORT IS A HOLE UNDER AUDIT WORLD5 C9: online a served sentence refills nothing (the clock is not this player's), and C9 was right about the free heal, but withholding the refill also withheld the FLOOR - so a player already at zero when the guards took them walked out of the cell dead, the death watcher raised death with no screen up, and the release ran again; the death screen owns input while up, which is why no menu would open. Offline keeps the full refill; online gets a floor that only moves health at or below zero. THE FAULT WAS NEVER ONE CALL SITE - it was four, each restoring health on its own (the online respawn, Privateer's Hold, an online load of a dead save, the prison release), and the pins sweep all four rather than trusting one. THE LOOP IS DRIVEN, not the wiring: a pin reading "reviveForPlay is called" would have passed against the shipped bug too, because the shipped bug called a heal as well - so the pins revive and THEN tick the drains and require the player alive on the other side. Also carries the F11 row (Janome: "in the exe version, F11 is the hotkey for full screen... so instead of making the game full screen it just loaded my save") - F9 QuickSave and F11 QuickLoad are DFU's own SetupDefaults, so the GAME's binding is correct and the SHELL gives way: Electron's `togglefullscreen` role carries F11 on Windows and Linux, and its accelerator moves to Alt+Enter (mac keeps Ctrl+Cmd+F, which collides with nothing), with a law that no shell accelerator may name a key DEFAULT_BINDINGS spends. He was exactly right: `died` in player/eotbBody.js is a LATCH raised from the live signal that then blocks every update, and the ONLY thing that lowers it is `initialize`, whose only caller is `toggle` going active - which is what scrolling out of first person and back in does. The port revives a MODULE-LEVEL body instead (a quickload back into play, the online respawn, a prison release) and none of those is an Initialize. A documented divergence from EOTB-IL in an otherwise IL-verbatim file. AND DEATHLOOP2, WHICH IS THE HALF DEATHLOOP1 LEFT OUT (DragynDance: "do you know why my game keeps spamming a wailing sound at me?", beside "I almost died in privateers hold due to freezing to death" and "as soon as I stepped outside my health bar started draaaaining"). DEATHLOOP1 ended the effect drains (poison, continuousDamage, transferHealth) and STOPPED THERE; the cold is not an effect at all - needs.js computes the felt temperature fresh every tick from climate, month, hour, weather, what is worn, how WET it is and the race (an Argonian carries RACE_TEMP -10, coldest of eight) - so a frozen character revived at half health in the same weather, still soaked, exposure counter still full, took the same killing tick again before they could walk anywhere. THE LETHALITY IS THE DESIGN AND IS LEFT ALONE, pinned so the next reader does not 'fix' it: needs.js withholds the health floor from that harm on purpose ('the bare-skin harms leave the last five points BECAUSE they are not meant to kill, and this one is'). ## PY1 - THE PARITY PINS WERE BLIND (2026-08-28)

**Fourteen pins across eight files were reporting green by never
running.** They are not remembered-value pins - they REGENERATE a port
table from Daggerfall Unity's own C# and compare it cell for cell:
ENEMY_BASICS off `EnemyBasics.cs`, LOOT_MATRICES off `LootTables.cs`,
the ingredient ITEM_GROUPS and artifact rows off `ItemEnums.cs`,
MAGIC_ONLY_KEYS off the effect classes, the race templates,
PlayerActivate's ladder, the two enemy-motor waves,
`DaggerfallInterior`, and MacroHelper's whole %-table. They are the
ONLY pins that can catch the port drifting from a DFU nobody re-read.

Every one resolved the checkout as a hardcoded `'../tools/parity/dfu/'`
and skipped when it was absent - which is every environment where the
reference tree lives somewhere else, including the one this project is
developed in (the clone sits outside the repo). The suite printed
`# skipped 14`, which at a glance reads exactly like `# pass 14`.

`tools/parity/prepare.sh` has honoured `DFU_PATH` since AUDIT 18 ("Point
it at a checkout you already have"); the tests simply never learned the
convention. `test/dfuRoot.mjs` is the one home now - env var first, the
in-tree sparse clone second, prepare.sh's own precedence - and with no
checkout at all the pins still skip, correctly: Port-Doctrine keeps DFU
an EXTERNAL reference, never vendored, so CI's shape is unchanged.

**All fourteen pass against the live checkout**, so the tables had not
drifted - the pins were right and blind, not wrong. Run them with:

```sh
DFU_PATH=/path/to/daggerfall-unity npm test
```

THE LESSON, and it is why this got its own slice: a skip is not a pass,
and a suite that cannot tell you which it printed is lying by omission.
The campaign taught the second half - the first version of the
env-var pin GREPPED the helper for `process.env.DFU_PATH`, and the
mutant that disabled the arm with `false ?` left the matched text
intact and survived. The pin spawns a child with the variable set and
asks where the root actually landed. **A pin that greps for a mechanism
does not test the mechanism.**

Pins: 3 in `test/parityroot.test.js` (a SOURCE SWEEP so no future test
re-hardcodes the path - the shape R6's bare-`this` sweep takes - plus
the behavioural precedence pin and the still-skips-cleanly arm).
Campaign: 5 mutants, 5 killed.

## EF1 - A COVERAGE CLAIM MUST BE MEASURED FROM BOTH SIDES (2026-08-28)

PY1's sibling, and the same failure one level up: PY1 was a pin that
never ran, this is a measurement that never asked the second question.

The effect library's `out.skipped++` had carried "the library grows one
family at a time" since the port's first magic slice, and it was picked
as the next slice on the strength of that one sentence. Three
measurements later there was no gap - and a defect the gap question
could not see.

**The first measurement used a proxy.** `effectActiveIdentity` was
asked which families it could name and answered "65 reached, 17
skipped". It is the ACTIVE-ENTRY classifier - an instant family handled
inline has no active identity by design - so Open, SpellAbsorption,
CreateItem and fourteen others were counted absent while sitting in the
file. A grep found all 17 in the port. The number was never reported as
a finding, because a number that measures the wrong thing is not a
weaker finding than the right one, it is not a finding.

**The second used the right instrument against the wrong corpus.** The
real counter, driven per key - but over a key set built by grepping
`MakeClassicKey(g, s)` for literals: 82 of DFU's 91.
`ElementalResistance.cs:194` and `PacifyEffect.cs:111` build theirs
from a loop variable, and nine real families are invisible to that
grep. Zero gaps against an incomplete corpus is not zero gaps, and the
mutation campaign now carries an arm that removes a single loop-keyed
variant (8,4) so a corpus that quietly loses them again fails.

**The third asked the other direction, and that is where the bug was.**
Sweeping all 65,536 classic keys through the real dispatcher, the port
answered 346 where DFU defines 91. The 255 extras were group 43,
subgroups 0-254: the Teleport arm tested `e.type === 43` and never its
subgroup, where DFU keys the class `MakeClassicKey(43, 255)`. Its own
comment read "(43,255)" the whole time.

THE LESSON: **"nothing is missing" and "nothing extra is answered" are
two claims, and a coverage pin that only makes the first will pass
forever on code that fails the second.** It was true on the broken
code. Whenever a pin asserts that some set is covered, ask what it says
about the things OUTSIDE the set - usually the answer is nothing, and
usually that is where the defect is.

The control arm is the other half of the discipline and costs four
lines: keys outside the classic space must REACH the counter. A
coverage pin whose measurement cannot report a miss proves nothing, and
the campaign's second mutant (delete `out.skipped++`) is exactly the
vacuous-measurement case it exists to catch.

Pins: 4 in `test/effectcoverage.test.js`. Two are UNGATED and catch the
defect in CI where no checkout exists; two REGENERATE DFU's key set
through `test/dfuRoot.mjs` (PY1's one home), so they run wherever the
tree is - and were verified against the live checkout, not left to
print a skip. Campaign: 5 mutants, 5 killed.
